commands.review_summary:
The PR centralizes mise data-directory resolution for PATH bootstrap, adding XDG and Windows defaults while treating whitespace-only `MISE_DATA_DIR` as unset.

PR surface: Source +22, Tests +74. Total +96 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. from source: set `MISE_DATA_DIR` to whitespace-only and compare OpenClaw’s proposed default fallback with mise’s `var_os`-based literal-path resolution. The PR’s Windows run confirms the altered OpenClaw path, though not the upstream-equivalence claim.
commands.review_followup: - A single mechanical correction can preserve the contributor’s Windows/XDG fallback work while aligning configured-value behavior with mise.

target.title: fix(path): retain mise shims when MISE_DATA_DIR is blank
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes child-process PATH construction when `MISE_DATA_DIR` is whitespace-only. The fallback now matches mise's platform contract instead of always selecting the Unix data directory.

## Why This Change Was Made

mise documents this precedence for its data directory:

1. a nonblank `MISE_DATA_DIR`, preserved verbatim;
2. `XDG_DATA_HOME/mise` on every platform;
3. `%LOCALAPPDATA%\mise` on Windows;
4. `~/.local/share/mise` on Linux and macOS.

OpenClaw previously treated a whitespace-only override as a literal directory. The first revision fixed blank handling but still selected the Unix default on Windows. This revision centralizes the complete platform-aware rule while keeping mise shims in the existing user-writable, append-only PATH tier.

Upstream contract: https://mise.jdx.dev/configuration.html#mise-data-dir

## User Impact

Commands installed through mise remain discoverable in service and minimal-shell environments with a blank `MISE_DATA_DIR`, including normal Windows installations under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\mise\shims`.

## Evidence

Exact head: `1c7d125746aeae0ab19180380b8c95f4c6e1326c`

Focused regression command:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/path-env.test.ts -- -t mise

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       4 passed | 20 skipped (24)
```

The four focused cases prove:

- blank Unix fallback to `~/.local/share/mise`;
- blank Windows fallback to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\mise`;
- `XDG_DATA_HOME/mise` precedence on Windows;
- literal preservation of a nonblank `MISE_DATA_DIR`, including boundary whitespace.

Targeted `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` passed. The complete file also ran locally: all 22 non-Brew cases passed; two pre-existing Windows-host simulations of macOS Linuxbrew behavior failed outside the changed mise surface. The repository CI run is the Linux truth for those platform-simulation cases.

### Real Windows production proof

Ran the exact head above on Windows through the production `ensureOpenClawCliOnPath` export. The proof created a temporary standard `%LOCALAPPDATA%\mise\shims` directory and a real `.cmd` shim, set `MISE_DATA_DIR` to whitespace with `XDG_DATA_HOME` absent, then used Windows `where.exe` and `cmd.exe` against the resulting PATH.

Copied redacted terminal output:

```text
platform=win32
MISE_DATA_DIR=<whitespace>
LOCALAPPDATA=<temp-root>\AppData\Local
XDG_DATA_HOME=<absent>
shim_appended=true
where_exit=0
where_result=<temp-root>\AppData\Local\mise\shims\openclaw-proof.cmd
command_exit=0
command_output=OPENCLAW_MISE_WINDOWS_LIVE
```

The temporary directory and shim were removed after the run. This verifies the documented Windows layout, production PATH mutation, native executable resolution, and real child-process execution rather than only a mocked filesystem assertion.
